text:
“Living without your caresses is great desolation;
living without your words is great solitude;
living without your loving gaze, ingenuous and clear,
is great darkness…”


I return, pale bride, whom you used to await
my return so early in the morning,
with the same song you preferred
and the same tenderness of other days
and the same love as always, to your window.


And I choose to see you, in delicate
complicity with Nature,
an afternoon like this: fainting
on a bed of lilacs, and imbued
with a certain aristocratic sadness.


I return to you with fingers intertwined
in an attitude of supplication and yearning
—as always—and lips untired
of praising you, and eyes obstinate
in seeing yours through the sky!


Receive me calmly, without rancor,
showing the soft manner of a sister;
murmur a peaceful “I forgive you,”
and let me sleep in abandon,
in your noble lap, until tomorrow….

translation.title: The Return
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the opening quotation and the returner’s repeated five-line appeals, with “deje suave de una hermana” rendered as a sister’s soft manner.
